articles.title: Where did Williams’ $1M worth F1 car go? Team sues garage owner for $1M+ after Ralf Schumacher historic car’s mystery disappearance
articles.summary: Williams is taking legal action against former garage owner Peter Thorpe after a historic Formula 1 car allegedly disappeared.
articles.body: Williams is taking legal action against former garage owner Peter Thorpe after a historic Formula 1 car allegedly disappeared. The British team is seeking £1 million ($1.34 million) from Thorpe for the return of its rare FW23, valued at £750,000 ($1.01 million). The car was driven by Ralf Schumacher and Juan Pablo Montoya during the 2001 F1 season.The FW23 was loaned to Autotech Performance Ltd in 2015. It was supposed to be displayed at the company’s garage in Telford. Williams later asked for the car to be returned, but the team says it received no response. Autotech has since been liquidated and dissolved.Williams seeks return of its missing FW23 car or $1.3 millionWilliams says the FW23 is part of its unique collection of heritage Formula 1 cars. Only nine examples of the car were manufactured. The team claims it strictly controls the use and sale of its historic cars to help preserve them.According to Williams’ court case, the team loaned the car to Autotech in 2015 under a “Historic Car Loan Agreement.” The agreement allowed the company to keep the car until October 2021.Williams then contacted Autotech that year and asked to inspect the car. The team also terminated the loan. However, it says there was no response.Williams’ lawyers claim the car was later removed from the garage. They allege Thorpe wrongly told a valuer working on Autotech’s liquidation that he personally owned the vehicle.“The car is part of the claimant’s unique collection of its own heritage cars, the use or sale of which it strictly controls inter alia [among other things] to ensure so far as possible that they are preserved”, Williams’ barrister Richard Clegg said while setting out the claim in the case papers.He added, “In 2015, the claimant agreed to loan the car to Autotech on the terms of a document entitled “Historic Car Loan Agreement” which terms were known and agreed to by Autotech.”Williams also claims the car remained at the company’s premises until its voluntary liquidation. The team says the vehicle was removed sometime after the liquidation process began.Thorpe, however, strongly disputes the allegations. He says he does not know where the car is and denies telling anyone that he owned it.His lawyer Duncan MacPherson said, “He does not know who in fact owned the car then or now. The defendant closed the business of Autotech on 30 June 2021. The defendant suffered a stroke on 7 October 2018 that caused him cognitive impairment,”Thorpe says he last saw the FW23 at the premises on August 8, 2021, when Autotech’s assets were being valued.His defence states, “The defendant admits that the car was at the premises on 8 August 2021, but does not admit whether it remained there until December 2021, because this lies outside his knowledge.”He also said he “believes that he has not told anyone that he owned the car, because he knew this to be untrue”.The case was filed at the High Court in London. It has not yet reached a full trial. Williams said it has “full faith in the legal system” to resolve the dispute.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “We’re committed to helping find a cure”: Triple H and wife Stephanie McMahon’s Pittsburgh fund Connor’s Cure raises $4.6M for 500 families
articles.summary: Triple H and his wife Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure in 2014 to honor late WWE fan, Connor Michalek.
articles.body: Triple H and his wife Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure in 2014 to honor late WWE fan, Connor Michalek. The Pittsburgh-based fund supports pediatric cancer research and families worldwide.Connor was diagnosed with medulloblastoma at age 3. He inspired the WWE fraternity through his unbreakable courage and unforgettable connection to his hero and retired professional wrestler, Daniel Bryan.The Connor’s Cure initiative partnered with UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh, and later with The V Foundation. Together, they could fund groundbreaking pediatric cancer research, including studies on DIPG [childhood diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma] and solid tumors.Through these futuristic efforts, Connor’s Cure has raised more than $4.6 million and helped over 500 families worldwide since its launch in April 2014. Stephanie McMahon and husband Triple H founded Connor’s Cure to honor Connor MichalekConnor’s Cure was inspired by Pittsburgh native Connor Michalek. When he was 3 years old, he was diagnosed with medulloblastoma, a tumor of the brain and spinal cord. He received a lifetime amount of radiation and underwent several surgeries. Doctors gave him a 0% chance of survival. He began clinical trials.In October 2012, a YouTube video of Michalek went viral in which he requested to meet his hero, then-WWE professional wrestler Daniel Bryan.Hundreds of people joined a Facebook group called “Help Connor meet Daniel Bryan.” Within 2 days, then-WWE chairman and CEO Vince McMahon responded that Bryan would meet Michalek.Twice, they met - once in December 2012 and a second time in October 2013. Michalek became a regular fixture at subsequent WWE events. WWE invited him to WrestleMania XXX. He scored a pinfall victory over Triple H and saw Bryan win the WWE World Heavyweight Championship in early April 2014.In late April 2014, Michalek passed away at the age of 8. He left a lasting impression on everyone he met in the WWE sphere. He was known for a quick wit and infectious grin. He melted even the toughest hearts of the WWE superstars and divas.Stephanie McMahon and her husband Paul Levesque became passionate about pediatric cancer research after meeting WWE superfan Connor “The Crusher” Michalek.A month after Connor passed away, Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure fund at Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh to honor his irreplaceable spirit.The WWE and Connor’s Cure raise funds to support pediatric cancer research. Donations to Connor’s Cure fund pediatric brain and spinal cancer research and medical care for children and their families.In 2016, Connor’s Cure raised almost $1 million. That same year, Connor’s Cure and UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh grew their partnership by joining forces with The V Foundation for Cancer Research. This partnership continued to drive research breakthroughs so no child would suffer as much as Connor Michalek did.Following The V Foundation’s partnership, support from the Connor’s Cure fund expanded nationwide to additional prominent researchers and cancer centers desperately seeking a cure for pediatric cancer.The UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh was named to the prestigious U.S. News & World Report Best Children’s Hospitals Honor Roll for 2026-2027.The hospital earned a place in the nation’s top 10 pediatric hospitals.The hospital also ranked in all 11 pediatric specialties surveyed. The hospital leads the nation in pediatric care, research, innovation, and education.WWE and The V Foundation advance the fight against childhood cancerThe V Foundation for Cancer Research, a top-rated cancer research charity, announced $16.2 million in funding awarded to 18 exceptional scientists through its Dick Vitale Pediatric Cancer Research Fund.Vitale and WWE have combined their efforts to fund three pediatric V Foundation Translational Grants totaling $1.8 million. Of that amount, Vitale and WWE contributed $900,000.Translational Grants are three-year awards totaling $600,000. They support bench-to-bedside research. Two of the grants will fund studies related to DIPG [childhood diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma], a universally fatal brain cancer. The third grant will fund research for solid tumors in children.“We’re thrilled to team with Dick Vitale to help further critical research and studies that are necessary in the fight against pediatric cancer,” Stephanie McMahon said via The V Foundation website.“Through WWE’s partnership with The V Foundation and in honor of Connor Michalek, we are committed to continue helping find a cure and will not stop until we do.”“Words cannot describe the excitement and joy I am feeling learning that Stephanie McMahon and her WWE team have united with us in providing funding that will play a vital role in battling pediatric cancer,” Dick Vitale said.“It is simply amazing what they are doing to attack the cancers that have caused nightmares for many youngsters and their families. These grants are made possible by the generosity of WWE and the kindness and generosity of those who have donated to our gala.We feel confident that these research grants will make a difference in the outcome for children with cancer.”The V Foundation has awarded more than $250 million for cutting-edge cancer research, holds a four-star rating from Charity Navigator, and is among the top 3% of all charities evaluated.WWE has also produced the “Support Tomorrow’s Superstars” campaign for pediatric patients undergoing treatment, supporting children fighting cancer.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is DonnaJean Wilde? Meet the 61-year-old grandmother who broke the women’s plank world record with a 5-hour hold
articles.summary: DonnaJean Wilde apparently decided four and a half hours in a plank was not enough.
articles.body: DonnaJean Wilde apparently decided four and a half hours in a plank was not enough.The 61-year-old Canadian grandmother has reportedly raised her own mark to five hours, according to the World Senior Games. Wilde previously earned Guinness World Records recognition after holding an abdominal plank for four hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds in March 2024.Who is DonnaJean Wilde, the 61-year-old grandmother behind the 5-hour plank world record?Wilde is a former high school vice principal and teacher from Alberta, Canada. She is also a mother of five and grandmother of 12.Her connection with planking started long before world records entered the picture.According to Guinness World Records, Wilde began planking after suffering a wrist injury that prevented her from running or lifting weights. She found that the static exercise was something she could still perform.Wilde later told Impact Magazine that the injury changed the direction of her training."I couldn't run. I could hardly walk down the road with a sling, but I could plank. It was such a pivotal moment for me that day. It just changed my life," she said.Her family eventually began testing how long she could stay in the position. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Wilde reached two hours.That result pushed the challenge into much more serious territory.She began structured preparation for the record in 2023. Her training included planks, running, weight lifting and push-ups, according to Impact Magazine.On March 21, 2024, Wilde held a plank for four hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds at Magrath High School, her former workplace.Guinness World Records recognized the performance as the longest time in an abdominal plank position by a woman. She beat the previous record, held by fellow Canadian Dana Glowacka, by more than 10 minutes.Wilde told Guinness that even after completing the attempt, the result was difficult to process."I actually still can't believe it," she said. "It feels like a dream."Two years later, the World Senior Games reported that Wilde had pushed the mark even further with a five-hour plank.How did DonnaJean Wilde train her body to hold a plank for five hours?Five hours did not come from doing planks alone.Wilde has said she uses several forms of strength training, including push-ups, weight lifting and running. She has also added dead hangs to her routine.In an Instagram post about upper-body strength, Wilde said she performs hundreds of push-ups and credited dead hangs with improving her grip.That matters because Wilde has dealt with chronic pain and numbness in her hands. Guinness previously reported that she lives with discomfort in her hands and arms.Her training volume before the 2024 record was far beyond a normal fitness routine. Guinness reported that Wilde sometimes practiced planking for as long as six hours per day while preparing for the attempt.And the plank is not her only record-setting exercise.In 2024, Wilde completed 1,575 push-ups in 60 minutes, breaking the existing record of 1,207 at the time. That mark has since been surpassed, according to Women’s Health.Her approach also comes with an important distinction. Wilde has trained for extreme endurance over several years. Her routine is not a starting point for an average person trying to improve core strength.Wilde’s own advice is much simpler."Keep trying and keep practicing," she told Guinness after her 2024 plank record.At 61, she is apparently still following it herself.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is Roxanne Perez’s boyfriend? All about WWE star’s relationship with Drake Moreaux, their relationship and more
articles.summary: Roxanne Perez has become one of WWE’s most talked-about female wrestlers after making a strong impact in NXT and later joining the main roster.
articles.body: Roxanne Perez has become one of WWE’s most talked-about female wrestlers after making a strong impact in NXT and later joining the main roster. Outside the ring, Perez has also attracted attention for her relationship with fellow professional wrestler Beau Morris. Morris is better known to wrestling fans by his ring names Drake Moreaux and El Carnicero. The couple has shared glimpses of their relationship on social media, while also supporting each other’s wrestling careers.Perez and Morris have been linked publicly since around Christmas 2024. Morris has been part of the WWE system since 2023 and has worked NXT events, house shows and dark matches. He also made an appearance in WWE LFG. Meanwhile, Perez has established herself as a major WWE star and a former two-time NXT Women’s Champion.Who is Roxanne Perez dating?Beau Morris is a professional wrestler who performs under the names Drake Moreaux and El Carnicero. He has been part of WWE’s system since 2023 and has spent several years working toward a bigger opportunity in the company.Morris has also competed outside WWE. He has worked with AAA, where he recently attracted attention after appearing as a masked attacker involved in a storyline surrounding Psycho Circus. AAA’s Verano de Escandalo week three, a mystery wrestler attacked Psycho Clown during a qualifier for the fatal four-way match for the vacant Latin American Championship at TripleMania 34. The masked wrestler attacked Clown while he was outside the ring and later ripped off his mask before chokeslamming him into a row of chairs.AAA did not immediately reveal the attacker’s identity. However, fans on social media quickly speculated that the wrestler was Drake Moreaux.Morris has been developing his career inside WWE for several years. He made his Evolve debut in 2025 and has also worked dark matches and house shows for NXT.He was also featured in WWE LFG. During the show, Morris spoke about his long wait for a major opportunity. He discussed watching friends and colleagues progress in the wrestling business while he continued to work toward his own breakthrough.His relationship with Perez has also become known among wrestling fans. The couple reportedly went public around Christmas 2024. Since then, they have frequently shared moments involving each other on social media.They also support one another professionally. Perez has been seen backing Morris during his wrestling appearances, while Morris has supported her career as she has continued to rise through WWE.Perez, whose real name is Carla Gonzalez, began wrestling at a young age. She trained under Booker T and made her professional debut in 2018 as Rok-C. She later became the inaugural ROH Women’s World Champion before signing with WWE in 2022.In WWE, Perez became a two-time NXT Women’s Champion and also won the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship with Cora Jade. She later moved to the main roster and joined The Judgment Day in 2025.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
